block.label: /block/<height>
block.proven: etherscan and every fork, blockscout, mempool.space and litecoinspace, Solana Explorer, Subscan, Starkscan, allo.info, Lora, HashScan, Aptos Explorer, EOS Authority, xmrchain — the common shape, and by far the most watched

blocks.label: /blocks/<height>
blocks.proven: mintscan — proven by cosmos/chain-registry's own block_page on COSMOSHUB, which is what lets its other deployments reuse it

checkpoint.label: /checkpoint/<n>
checkpoint.proven: Suiscan, IOTA Explorer — Sui and IOTA count checkpoints, and a checkpoint number is what the router reports as their latest block

ledger.label: /ledger/<sequence>
ledger.proven: xrpscan, stellar.expert — a ledger sequence is this family's block height

slot.label: /slot/<slot>
slot.proven: beaconcha.in — the consensus layer counts slots, which is what the router reports as a beacon spec's latest block

root.label: /<height>
root.proven: tzkt — one root namespace resolves levels, operation hashes and addresses alike

hash-routed.label: /#/block/<height>
hash-routed.proven: tronscan — client-side routing puts every path behind a #, which is part of the URL the browser needs

home.label: Home page only
home.proven: n/a — the explorer exists but no height-addressed block page has been proven for it. explorerBlockUrl() returns null and only the home URL is offered. A terminal state, not a TODO: an honest home link beats a block link that lands on an empty page.
